title: India Just Launched Its Biggest Rupee Rescue Since 2013. NRI Deposits Are at the Centre of It.
excerpt: The RBI and the Finance Ministry rolled out a coordinated package to attract $40-50 billion in dollar inflows. For NRIs, the subsidized FCNR deposit window that closes September 30 is the most actionable opportunity.
body:
On Friday, June 5, the Reserve Bank of India held its policy rate at 5.25 per cent and did something far more consequential. In coordination with the Finance Ministry, it launched the most aggressive package of dollar-attraction measures India has deployed since the taper tantrum of 2013.

The rupee has lost more than 6 per cent against the dollar this year, breaching 95 to the dollar for the first time. Foreign portfolio investors have pulled out over ₹2.47 lakh crore since January — more than double the total outflow for all of 2025. The Middle East war has pushed crude past $90 a barrel, swelling India's import bill. The balance of payments deficit for FY27 is projected at $40-50 billion.

The measures announced Friday are designed to close that gap. Analysts at HDFC Bank, YES Bank, and Emkay Global estimate they could attract $40-60 billion within months.

## What Changed, in Plain Terms

**Capital gains tax on government bonds: gone.** Foreign portfolio investors are now exempt from capital gains tax on interest income and trading gains from Indian government securities, effective retroactively from April 1. Previously, short-term gains were taxed at 30 per cent and long-term gains at 12.5 per cent. The 20 per cent withholding tax on interest from government bonds has also been scrapped.

**FCNR deposits: subsidized.** The RBI will bear the full hedging cost for banks that raise three-to-five-year Foreign Currency Non-Resident deposits until September 30. This is the measure that matters most for NRIs. When banks do not have to pay for hedging the currency risk, they can offer higher interest rates on dollar-denominated deposits. The deposits are also exempt from the statutory liquidity ratio and cash reserve ratio requirements, making them cheaper for banks to hold.

**Concessional forex swaps for state-owned companies.** The RBI will offer discounted forex swap facilities to public sector enterprises raising funds through external commercial borrowings until September 30. This reduces the cost of dollar borrowing for companies like ONGC, Indian Railways, and NTPC.

**Wider foreign access to government bonds.** All new 15-year, 30-year, and 40-year government bonds will be included in the Fully Accessible Route, which allows unfettered foreign investment and is part of three major global bond indexes. Caps on short-term foreign investment in bonds, concentration limits, and restrictions on buying individual bonds have been removed.

## What NRIs Should Do Right Now

The FCNR deposit window is the most time-sensitive opportunity. Here is why it matters and what to consider:

FCNR deposits are dollar-denominated fixed deposits held at Indian banks. You deposit dollars and receive dollars back at maturity — there is no currency risk for the depositor. The interest rate is set by the bank, typically benchmarked to LIBOR or SOFR plus a spread.

With the RBI now absorbing the hedging cost, banks can afford to offer higher rates on three-to-five-year FCNR deposits than they normally would. The subsidy window runs until September 30, 2026, which means deposits opened before that date lock in the benefit for the full tenure.

For an NRI sitting on dollar savings or contemplating where to park a portion of a 401(k) rollover, the timing is specific. The effective yield on FCNR deposits is likely to be 50-100 basis points higher than normal during this window, depending on the bank and tenure.

Banks that have historically been aggressive on FCNR rates — SBI, Bank of Baroda, Bank of India, and Union Bank of India — are expected to raise rates within days to attract early inflows.

## The Macro Context: Why the RBI Did This

The measures are not charity for NRIs. They are a calculated move to defend the rupee without burning foreign exchange reserves or raising interest rates.

India's forex reserves have already declined from their peak, and defending the currency by selling dollars in the open market is expensive and unsustainable. Attracting dollars through deposits and bond investments is cheaper and longer-lasting.

The RBI raised its FY27 inflation forecast to 5.1 per cent — with Q3 inflation expected to hit 5.9 per cent, dangerously close to the 6 per cent upper band. GDP growth was revised down to 6.6 per cent from 6.9 per cent. Governor Sanjay Malhotra described the hold as a "strategic" one, but economists at Capital Economics expect cumulative rate hikes of 75 basis points by year-end, taking the repo rate to 6.00 per cent.

For NRIs, this macro picture has a direct implication: if rates do rise later this year, locking in FCNR deposits now at the subsidized window rate could mean getting a better deal than waiting.

## The Bottom Line

India is under genuine external pressure — the kind it has not faced since 2013. The policy response is coordinated, aggressive, and specifically designed to channel diaspora dollars back into the system. The FCNR subsidy window is narrow (September 30), the yields are temporarily elevated, and the deposits carry zero currency risk for the NRI depositor.

If you have been meaning to put dollars to work in India, the next four months are the specific window the Reserve Bank of India has engineered for you.

*Sources: Reuters (June 5, 2026); Reserve Bank of India monetary policy statement (June 5, 2026); The Hindu BusinessLine; Wall Street Journal; Capital Economics*
